subject.title: fix(cron): respect deliveryBestEffort in interim-message suppression guard

question: Should `deliveryBestEffort` disable stale interim-message suppression for isolated cron jobs, or remain limited to tolerating outbound delivery failures?
rationale: Current main has an explicit regression expectation for suppression in this exact best-effort scenario, while the helper comment defines a narrower failure-tolerance contract; code review cannot safely choose the user-facing delivery policy.

options.title: Keep suppression independent
options.body: Retain the current test and reject this change so best-effort affects send-failure handling but still prevents stale descendant interim replies.

options.title: Expand best-effort semantics
options.body: Accept delivery of interim text in best-effort mode, then document the broadened contract and add cases that prove it does not create undesirable duplicate delivery.

recommendation.title: Keep suppression independent
recommendation.body: Retain the current test and reject this change so best-effort affects send-failure handling but still prevents stale descendant interim replies.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows repeated ownership of the affected cron delivery policy and adjacent behavior changes.
